title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: How does the generated command handler decide the command's permission on its resource before the fill?
description: ST-SUP-RC32-OC06 and ST-SUP-RP10-LC05 say that the handler decides the command's declared permission on the resource that the resource member names, at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, before the fill and in the command's one transaction (ST-SUP-RC32-OC04), and ST-SUP-RC32-OC06-T01 expects that decision at the consistency at_least t5, the authz_token of the row. The command runtime on main cannot do this: Run opens the transaction and calls the fill with no step between them; the handle reads only the entities that the command writes (ST-SUP-RP10-LC02), and the resource, such as Order, is not one of them; Authz.Evaluate takes only a loaded value of the handle; and the generated code reaches no transaction. Options: (A) add to the command runtime a resource of the command: CommandSpec gets the permission and a generated resource spec (its resource type, a Select of the ID and the authz_token that takes the tenant as $1, and ValidID), Request gets the resource ID, and Run reads the token and decides with the authorization handle in each attempt's transaction after the bind and before the idempotency wrapper, so a replay is decided too, and returns a new ErrDenied, which the handler answers with 403 and audits with the outcome denied; (B) the generator adds the resource's entity to the command's Writes, so the generated adapter reads it and calls Authz.Evaluate before the fill; this lets the fill write the resource (against ST-DECL-INV38) and adds a read decision; (C) the handler decides through the port before Run, at the floor only; this loses the row's token and is not in the transaction. Recommendation: A, because the decision is the same for every command, so ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05 puts it in the runtime, and the writes stay as declared. Until it is decided, the command generator emits no handler.

title: What are the members of a command's request and response?
description: ST-SUP-RC32-OC01 gives the fill the command's decoded request, ST-DECL-EN18 names a resource member of the request and a route with path parameters, and ST-SUP-RC32-OC10-T01 expects the status 201, but no record states the members of a command's request or what its fill returns: ST-DECL-EN18 has no request or response field, and only a command with a gRPC Method has a protobuf message. The generator cannot emit the slot contract, the decoder, the fingerprint or the response without them. Options: (A) every command names a protobuf request and response message, which a Method also uses: the HTTP route decodes the body with protojson and the path parameters into the request, and the fill returns the response message, which the handler answers with 201 for a command that creates and 200 for any other; (B) ST-DECL-EN18 gets typed request members and response members, as entity fields are typed, the path parameters of the route are request members, and the generator emits Go types with JSON names; a command with a Method maps them to its messages; (C) the request is the path parameters and the raw JSON body, and the fill returns a status and a body. Recommendation: A, because one message pair serves the HTTP route and the gRPC method with the same fill (ST-SUP-RC07-OC19), and the existing slot contracts are protobuf messages. Until it is decided, the command generator emits no slot contract or handler.
